utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Good morning, Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Accused Pandurevic is absent today as well, explanation was provided yesterday. The Prosecution team today is like yesterday, Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. Absent from the Defence teams, I notice Mr. Nikolic, Ms. Nikolic, Mr. Petrusic, Mr. Krgovic, and Mr. Haynes; but I have to keep looking because some of them could be behind the column. So the witness is here. Good morning, to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed and finish with your testimony. Mr. Thayer has -- how much more time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I believe I will need the hour I referred to yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just a couple of quick questions about some of your prior interviews. Before you came here to The Hague to testify, can you tell us how many times you met with the Borovcanin Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Mr. Lazarevic twice, and once I had a meeting with a lady, Ms. Or Mrs.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you recall when those interviews were? Just a year and a month would be fine?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps three months ago, I met with a gentleman and, then some 20 days ago, I met with both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you no doubt recall being interviewed by the investigators for SIPA, the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo in June of this year; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you just tell me, do you recall whether you met with the Borovcanin Defence team before you were interviewed which the SIPA team, after you were interviewed by the SIPA team, or before and after you were interviewed by the SIPA team?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met with Mr. Lazarevic before that interview once, and when I met with the two of them together, that was following the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "I met with the two of them together following the interview," I take it by that you mean you met with the two investigators from SIPA after you had met with Mr. Lazarevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. My question is - I'll just ask the question again - do you recall whether you met the investigators from the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo before or after you had met with Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met with the investigators after I had met with Mr. Lazarevic, and the interview with the investigators was before the meeting at which I met with Mr. Lazarevic and the lady.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer, what does the acronym SIPA stand for, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll get that. It's -- bear with me one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Explain to us what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It stands with the agency that's charged with investigating war crimes. I can't remember the exact title.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In Bosnia, that's correct, based in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified that Radomir Pantic was the commander of the 1st Company Zvornik PJP yesterday, and there were six companies in total; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the company commander, and there were five or six, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who within the PJP formation was Mr. Pantic's commander in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantic's commander and superior was Mr. Danilo Zoljic, aka Daca.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just for the record, sir, do you know what Mr. Zoljic's occupation or position was, if any, outside of his role within the PJP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that he commanded the joint detachment comprising those companies at the level of the centre. He commanded all six companies, if there were six, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I'm just going to ask you a couple of questions to see whether you can help us put names to a couple of faces. And if I understand correctly, whereas the third platoon of the 1st Company Zvornik PJP was comprised of police officers from various police stations, such as Milici, Bratunac, Sekovici, Vlasenici, Skelani, the first platoon was comprised mostly, if not entirely, of Zvornik police officers. Do I have that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you referred yesterday to an officer with the surname Ikonic being deployed near you at Sandici; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood properly. Officer Ikonic?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. You referred yesterday to -- by last name to somebody named Ikonic being deployed with you in your area in Sandici; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Policeman Ikonic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's right. When I say "officer," I mean police officer, sir. I apologise. Now, in your statement to the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo, you recalled that one of the colleagues who went with you on this mission was named Rista Ikonic. Is that the Ikonic where you were referring to yesterday, sir, a police officer from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Rista Ikonic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know another police officer from Zvornik by the name of Mile Savic? He now works for the border police, I think.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to very quickly show you a clip from a video and just see if you can put a name to a face.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could begin rolling the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm going to do is, we are going to freeze the frame at a certain point, and if it's too blurry, I have a photographic printout, just a still, to show you the old-fashioned way if we need it. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've paused the clip at 2 hours 38 minutes and 7 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you need the sound or not because I didn't get -- do you need sound because I didn't get any sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, that's okay, Mr. President, we don't need sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, let me just hand you - with Madam Usher's assistance - a still that was taken from that. It might be a little better. I just want to ask you: There's an individual to the left who looks a little bit younger than the man in the right of this photograph. Do you recognise the man on the left?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We are done with this clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just want to show you quickly one other clip and see if you can put a name to a face for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this location is the meadow in Sandici or across from the meadow in Sandici, near the destroyed white house that I think you have referred to previously. We don't have the audio, but there's somebody calling out to Mile, and let me show you the still because it captures an individual. Let me hand you the video still, sir. Here we go. Now, we've paused at 2 hours, 52 minutes, 32.2 seconds. Sir, there are two individuals depicted in this video still. The individual on the far right has ID'd himself as Mile Savic. My question is: Either from looking at the still on the screen or the photograph that I've handed to you, can you identify the individual in the middle? There's another man wearing a green camouflage uniform immediately to the left of Mr. Savic. Can you recognise that individual?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We are done with that. Now, yesterday, you told us, sir, that your platoon formed up in front of the Zvornik police station between 6.00 and 7.00, in the evening. Can you confirm what you told the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo; namely, that it was your platoon komandir, Cvijan Ristic, who told you that you were going to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you testified yesterday that you were billeted in a sports hall or a school somewhere in Bratunac. Can you tell the Trial Chamber, as best as you can remember, where that sports hall or school was located?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain. I think it is as one enters Bratunac and moves towards the police station, and then it would be to the right; basically, vis-a-vis the police station on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And is it before the police station as you enter Bratunac, or do you have to pass the police station to get to this location?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think it was before, although I'm uncertain, because we were on foot and I saw that we passed by the police station at some point. We went there to spend the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall where in relation to the Hotel Fontana this location was, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where the Hotel Fontana is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the answer that the witness gave to the question of my colleague is not properly recorded. It's on page 7: "... because we were on foot and I saw that we passed by the police station at some point. We went there to spend the night." What I believe, well, the witness said that: "We were in front of the police station and then we went on foot to this location." This was my understanding of what he said, but, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You can clarify it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you heard what my learned friend just said. Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were in front of the police station and went on foot to spend the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you testified yesterday that it was about 0400 hours on the 12th of July when your company formed up in front of Commander Pantic in Bratunac. Can you confirm what you told the Prosecutor's office in Sarajevo that there were between 50 and 60 PJP officers present at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 50 policemen, three platoons; between 50 and 60, that would be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you testified yesterday about receiving your concrete task that morning to scour the terrain and engage in combat if you encountered armed groups; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's fair to say that this was a potentially dangerous operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a combat task to search the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you had information that there might be individuals or groups of individuals who were armed in this location you were going to scour; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that there is a possibility to encounter such a group or individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall telling the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo that Pantic told you that there was danger?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was danger that could have been posed by a group. Any such a group or individual would pose a threat to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the gathering at Zuti Most. If I understand your testimony, Pantic, Stuparevic, and Ristic were all present when you were at Zuti Most; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of Zuti Most, in the area of Zuti Most; correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, approximately what time was this when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe around 5.00 or 5.30 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 4.30 or 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were there any other Serb forces at Zuti Most? Any other PJP units, special police brigade members, army?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no one in our environs save for our group.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was it your understanding, sir, that other than the deminer and anybody that he was with, that you were and your fellow PJP officers were the first Serb officers to arrive at Zuti Most and enter Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't believe this is a fair question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a compounds question. First: "... you were and your fellow PJP officer were the first officer to arrive at Zuti Most," that is one question, "and enter Potocari," that's another question. I think it's a compounds question, and the witness should answer one and then maybe another one. My colleague should split it in two.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No problem, Mr. President, I'd be happy so do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he can answer the question. It's not compounded at all. So let's answer the question, Witness, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And, furthermore, he never said in his testimony that they enter Potocari, in the early morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll just take it one step at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, was it your understanding that you and your fellow PJP officers were the first Serb forces to arrive at Zuti Most that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we got to the area in front of Zuti Most. I don't know who controlled the territory. Well, I assumed that we were in the territory controlled by our forces. That's when we got there, but there was nobody else there, not army. I didn't see any other troops there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And was it your understanding that you and your fellow PJP officers would be the first Serb forces to descend towards the UN base in Potocari as you told us yesterday you did?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question, it's not quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question is, sir: Was it your understanding that you and your PJP unit were the first Serb forces to enter the area that you told us yesterday you scoured that day on 12 July, that there was no other Serb forces that entered that area that day or the previous day?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my understanding that we were the first unit to scour or search that area. Well, I am not familiar with the area. I don't know what parts of Potocari there are, upper, lower, "gornji," "donji." It was my understanding that we would be the first units to conduct the search operation around Potocari of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you told us that your platoon commander, Mr. Ristic, was basically next to you during the course of this search. Do you recall what other Serb units were on your side of the road during this entire period of time that you scoured the terrain?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, there were no other units there, apart from our company.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How about on the other side of that road that passes in front of the UN compound between Bratunac and Srebrenica, who was on the other side of that road scouring the terrain as you were on the right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, yesterday, you were asked whether you had any special orders with regard to the civilians, and you responded, at page 26928, for my friends: "If we were to come across civilians, we were not to pay any attention to them. We should just proceed and mind our own business, so to speak." Then you later said: "We even had an order from our company commander not to approach them and not to mingle, not to mix with them." Now, sir, in your interview with SIPA --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I've been advised by higher levels that that stands for State Investigation and Protection Agency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In your interview with SIPA in June of this year, sir, you were asked the following question regarding the task you were given when you arrived at Zuti Most, and this is at page 33 of the interview. "Q. And were you told what to do if you confronted any armed groups?" Your answer: "No, nothing was said to us in that respect. We were just told to search the terrain." "Q. Were you instructed at the time what to do if you came across any civilians? "A. No, nothing." On the next page of the interview, you were asked, sir: "Q. What were you expect today do if you detained any persons who were members of armed groups? "A. So in case we encountered such persons, if we ever had those persons open their fire against us, then we would have probably returned fire; but in all other cases, we were supposed to report to our commander, to advise our commander." Then you were asked this follow-up question right away, it's the next question: "And what would be expected of you if you came across civilians?" And your answer, sir, was: "We did not have any specific instruction in that sense, but I guess we would be also expected to inform our commander." Now, sir, you were very clear yesterday that you received a specific order from your commander basically to just walk on by civilians if you encountered them during this terrain search; but as we just heard, just a couple of months ago in June, you were equally clear that you received no specific instructions regarding civilians. Now, sir, there's nothing in the notes of your proofing with my friends regarding this order, so my question to you is: Was yesterday the first time you told anybody about this specific order to ignore the civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the essence remains the same. We got a task, it was a combat mission to search the terrain, and I said, these were my words, that we were not interested in civilians. At that time, I said that I had not received any specific instructions. To my mind, that's one in the same thing. So we didn't have any tasks to take care of civilians. It was just a plain and simple search operation. And as for this order not to approach civilians, this is what we got from our komandir once we got down to the tarmac road, if I understand your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just clarify your answer a little bit, sir, and I appreciate that. You just said that "... these were my words, that we were not interested in civilians." So I just want to make sure, is it your testimony, then, that prior to conducting the scouring of the terrain, Commander Pantic didn't actually give you any order to leave the civilians alone, that was just your approach to the situation, but you received no specific order at that time, as opposed to when you were down closer to the base to leave the civilians alone?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any specific orders from the komandir except for the order to carry out the search operation of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just ask you one follow-up question on the issue of civilians during the search, sir. I think you'll agree with me, especially in the war in Bosnia, a male of fighting age in civilian clothes might be a civilian, but he might very well be a soldier; right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's an armed civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm referring to just somebody that you encounter that doesn't have an obvious, say, automatic rifle on his shoulder, but somebody that is just dressed in civilian clothes, just wearing a civilian jacket, for example. Such a person could be a civilian or he could be a soldier, you just don't know, is that right, just by looking at him?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But when I talk about civilians, I mean women, children, people who are infirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it, then, if you encountered a male of fighting age, you would want to take steps to ensure that that male isn't armed in some fashion, that he doesn't have a pistol under his shirt or a grenade inside a jacket pocket; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, you referred to a house where you positioned yourself while the deming took place. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the house, not inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Understood. And as we saw from the photographs yesterday, there are houses, in some cases scattered and in some cases grouped together, along the way from Zuti Most down to the UN base. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what were your instructions regarding searching the houses?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't even start the search of the terrain from the houses and the road. That we started in front of the Zuti Most. As I explained yesterday, we went in a single file up there above the place where we were to start the search operation, and there was this house there. I don't recall. It was a lone house, if I'm not mistaken. It was just before we crossed the minefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. But my question was: What were your instructions, your orders regarding searching any houses that you encountered during the search of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told not to go into the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, in fact, according to what you told the investigators from SIPA, you did not enter any of the houses; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you explain, I'm a little confused on this issue, sir. You and your fellow PJP officers are trained police officers, you are told that this might be a dangerous operation because there were armed individuals or groups who may be in this area trying to break out, that you are specifically looking for during this operation. Weren't you concerned that there might be armed people concealed in one of those houses who might open fire against you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was logical to expect this; but like in all other combat missions, you just pass by any house very carefully using any cover that was available, including the trenches that they had dug between the houses. As far as the houses are concerned, I personally took the far right side along the edge of the wood where there were just a few houses, very few houses, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just follow-up on that, sir. Were you concerned that someone might open fire on you from any of those houses?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be natural for the order to be for people to search the houses and not be forced to rely on whatever cover might be nearby to make sure that those houses were cleared and pacified?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not receive any orders, or at least I don't know about it. But when I started the search operation, this was my understanding, that we were to search the terrain but we were not told that we were supposed to search the houses, if there were any around Potocari, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that Danilo Zoljic, Mr. Pantic's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise to my colleague. There is one piece of witness's answer which was not record. He said that he didn't even know there would be any houses in the area. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I thank my friend. I'm just going to move along.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that Danilo Zoljic, Mr. Pantic's PJP commander, testified in the Sarajevo trial of Milo Stupar, a special police brigade member of the 2nd Sekovici Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, he was asked in that trial on 15 September 2006, this is at page 28, regarding the morning of 12 July at Zuti Most, and I quote the question: "Did you receive some tasks from Ljubisa Borovcanin?" And Mr. Zoljic answered: "I asked Ljubisa what tasks were to be executed by the 1st Company of the special police unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think my friends will agree that that's a reference to the PJP and not the Special Police Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And Mr. Zoljic continued his answer: "Ljubisa Borovcanin said to all of us that the 1st Company and the 2nd Detachment were to search houses from Zuti Most towards Srebrenica, so a part of the Potocari settlement located on the right side of the road looking from the direction of Zuti Most towards Srebrenica. After the search of these houses is completed above the settlement, houses on the slope, so on the rising ground, hill." Now, he is try describing the area where you testified you scoured the terrain, isn't he, the right-hand side, on an elevation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Just for the record and to make sure that we are in agreement, this Ljubisa Borovcanin is not the accused, you agree on it, don't you; or are you referring to or is he referring to the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: He is refer together the accused, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But the accused is not Ljubisa, he is Ljubomir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I'm asking the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, he is referring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Due agree with this, Mr. Lazarevic, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do agree. Also, I don't think there is a basis for this question. I mean, I believe my colleague should have asked first whether he saw Mr. Zoljic, whether he can comment on this what Mr. Zoljic is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question was a legitimate one because it follows the previous answer of the witness; namely, that they had not received any instructions regarding searching houses, and his associate, or mate at the time, apparently testified differently in other proceedings. So let's proceed --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and if you could stick to what is relevant to the case and bring your cross-examination to the end, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President. I just note for the record that there are references signatures, typed signatures, from Mr. Borovcanin in which he refer toss himself as Ljubisa. His formal name is Ljubomir, but there are references to Ljubisa as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just said it for the record because I didn't want later on to find ourselves in a position where we didn't or we wouldn't know who the witness was referring to or who are you referring to. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, at page 32 of that transcript, Mr. Zoljic was asked: "Were you receiving reports regarding the search of houses from commander or his deputy?" And Mr. Zoljic answered: "Since I was on the road somewhere in the middle looking from Zuti Most, I did not insist on details. When the search has been completed, the commanding officer informed me by radio that there were neither civilians nor men fit for military service present in those houses." Then he continues that when the search was completed, Pantic informed him by radio of that fact. Now, sir, I put it to you that the PJP, in fact, did search houses that morning towards Potocari. Is it still your testimony that no one searched any houses?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was to the far right and I couldn't see what the others were doing; but if you pass by the house, that does not mean that you search the house. I did not got into any of the houses. You have house searches that you do normally once you have a search warrant. I did not enter a single house and the guys around me did not either.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall whether there were any dogs that were being used by any of the forces during this scouring?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since in our company we did not have people trained to handle dogs, apart from myself and my colleague, but he was not there, the dogs were not used. They were not present there. I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to share with you a couple of accounts from Dutch officers that were observing the events that morning of the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The first is from 65 ter 3800, an OTP witness statement of a Dutch officer named Rene van Kuijen, K-u-i-j-e-n. This is at page 3 of the English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm just going to read it to you, sir, to save some time. He said: "In the morning of the 12 July, I was on duty inside the compound at the designated locations for monitoring everything in and outside the compound coming within the site. I started my duty between 0600 and 0700 hours, and I was looking through the binoculars. I saw about 100 Serb soldiers in the northerly direction of the enclave. Some of them had German Shepherd dogs. Many Muslim houses were located on the northwesterly side of the road on the hills. I saw that Serb soldiers were systematically cleansing those houses. The soldiers would hurl a grenade inside the house, and I had the impression that they were killing the inmates of those houses without any warning. I saw that process having been repeated by them many times. I could not hear any shrieks or shouting from that direction as I was standing at some distance. I heard from my superiors that the soldiers with the dogs were the Drina Brigade and stationed somewhere in Bratunac." Before I put my question to you, sir, I just want to read another portion of an UN DutchBat officer's OTP witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's 65 ter 3797. It's a man named Jan Spek [phoen] Schneider.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: He said at page 2, and we only have an English version of this: "In the morning of 12 July, I was up quite early. The VRS soldiers started coming at about 10.00. I saw them from the compounds. First, I saw the group of such soldiers on the hills in northwesterly direction. They were dressed in green camouflage uniforms, and some of them had dogs. They were systematically cleansing the house located there. They would send the dog inside a house or, alternatively, throw a grenades in the house. I saw the inmates coming out of the house. I heard continue use shooting from that direction. I could not clearly see anything, but my impression was that the soldiers had been killing the inmates of those houses. I had this impression for another reason that I did not see any of those Muslims coming to the compound to take refuge with the others. The house were located in a northwesterly direction and of distance of about 300 to 500 metres from the compound." Now, again, sir, this sounds like the area that you were scouring. Is it your testimony that you saw none of the activities described by these two DutchBat officers during the entire time that you were participating in this scouring operation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that absolutely does not correspond to our unit. It has nothing to do, whatsoever, with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever become aware, sir, that any other unit performed any of those acts that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know about that, and I never heard about that subsequently either.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to turn your attention in the few minutes I have left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, you referred to the killing of people who were inside the houses. Are those part of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Those have not been charged, Your Honour, as opportunistic killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn your attention, sir, to your testimony yesterday that Commander Pantic told you that there was a UN checkpoint; and in your words, that you should pay special attention to it, be mindful of it, avoid any possible conflicts with the officers, any sort of communication. You specified, at 26938, that you had an order from your company commander not to approach UNPROFOR at any cost, not to engage in any combat, not to open fire in their direction, anything. Sir, did you ever hear that any PJP officers or special police brigade members went to the UN checkpoint near Yellow Bridge where the Dutch peacekeepers were that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to share with you, then, one final OTP witness statement from a Dutch officer, Roger Patelski.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This is 65 ter 3798.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps the witness could take off the headphones because I would like to address an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make sure if he understands English or not. Do you understand English at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please remove your headphones. Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my colleague is using statements that were shown to him by my colleague. If the purpose is to check his credibility, that's fine. But there are parts of those statements made by people who did not testify here, and the Defence cannot cross-examine them, yet this is now on the record. I don't know how the Trial Chamber will be able to give proper weight to those parts of the statements perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not evidence, so put your mind at rest that that is not where we are heading, so don't worry about it. But I understand, Mr. Thayer, what you are testing is the witness's credibility, first and foremost.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President, as we've said on numerous occasions, we offer our evidence at the end of the day for any purpose for which the Trial Chamber deems appropriate, but this is all about credibility, as I've said before, in other circumstances. This is about credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can't have the cake and eat it, too. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to say. They closed their case, Your Honour. This is something really unfair towards --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let us manage the whole matter. I mean, we have more than once explained to you what our position is, and we don't need to repeat it. Yes, let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to read to you a portion of this witness statement, and, unfortunately, we don't have a translation. So, bear with me, it's going to take just a little bit of time. At page 3 of the interview, this Dutch officer said: "I think it was 11 July when I heard on the radio that the Serbian troops were advancing from the south, and later they took on the enclave. The next day the troops around us also began to move in the direction of Potocari. Jovo called our OP and informed that the Serbian troops were beginning to move, and if we did not resist, we would not be harmed. I received that message, and as soon as I hung up, I saw the tanks moving from the surrounding of the Serbian command post towards the main asphalt road. It was around 1000 to 1100 hours in the morning of the next day of the fall of the enclave. The soldiers also moved along the side of the road. "The first troops appeared to be well trained army unit. They were dressed in cam collage uniforms and heavily armed. They were in hundreds. A group of 15 to 20 soldiers came to our OP. A young Serb soldier commanded the group. He had dark short hair, about 1.9 metres tall, and had reddish skin. They were all dressed in camouflage uniforms. The commander spoke good English. They seized our helmets, flak jackets and arms, and disconnected our contact with the OPs room, and put us in the corner. They seized our APC and asked the driver to explain its operation. "Sometime later, I managed to go to the tower of the OP. I saw that the few other groups of the Serb soldiers went towards the Muslim houses located on both sides of the roads. Such groups were dressed in black uniforms and had dogs with them. The black uniform was comprised of an overall and a black leather waist belt but no caps. They carried digital walkie-talkie sets. "They would go near the house and throw a grenade into it. After that, they would enter the house with dogs which, would be followed by shooting and screams. I knew that a number of Muslim people were still living in those houses. I had the impression that the people had been killed in the houses. I did not see anyone coming out of those houses. After that, the Serb soldiers would come out of the house and set it on fire. They would then move to the next house. "Another group of Serb soldiers proceeding in the direction of Potocari were dressed in blue camouflage uniforms. One such soldier was also present at our OP and had come with squad and captured our OP. Somebody asked him why he was wearing blue camouflage uniform and what was the difference between the normal camouflage and the blue. He replied that the soldiers dressed in blue camouflage uniform were a 'special police unit.' The soldiers in black overalls were a kind of anti-terrorist unit. "Another group, which walked passed the OP after the regular one's, were Rambo-type. They were dressed in a ninety-six tour of civilian and military gear and well armed with grenades, AK-47 and knives. "We were detained at the OP until 2100 hours that day. We were guarded all the time."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we have the question, Mr. Thayer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I had to read that whole section, Your Honour, because it's bounded on both sides by what happened at the OP and the events in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you heard what this DutchBat officer told the OP about Serb soldiers taking over that observation point. I ask you again: Did you ever hear any information that PJP officers, special police brigade, or any Serb forces took over that Dutch checkpoint near Zuti Most that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am completely not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, taking you down closer to the UN base, you testified that when you descended towards it, you ended up about 150 to 200 metres, and that you could see the large group of refugees well from your position. Do you recall how far you were from the entrance to the actual compound, to the Dutch base compound?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see it full well, but I could see a group there. I was some 200 metres or 150 metres to the left from the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So, just to be clear, you could see the actual entrance to the compound; is that what you are telling the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see those gathered there. I don't remember the very entrance, but we were close to the base and I could see the people inside. I could see those assembled.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, in your interview in Sarajevo, you said that Commander Pantic wanted to keep you together as a group and not to disperse. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, again, as you testified yesterday, you even had this order, you said, not to approach the civilians, and you affirm that this morning, that that is what the actual order regarding civilians was?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslim civilians boarding buses to take them away, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the group of people, but I did not see any buses. The people were still arriving.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslim --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. The answer was improperly recorded. Here, we have on page 27, lines 7 to 8: "I saw the group of people. But I did not see any buses." No, that's not what the witness said. Maybe he can repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Could you repeat the answer, please, because we've got a problem with the transcript. What did you see? Did you see the people? Did you see the Muslim civilians boarding buses to be taken away? What is your answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw the people gathered in front of it, but I did not see any boarding of the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, did you see any Muslim males being separated from their families while you were at your position?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you testified yesterday that, and I quote: "We encountered a few empty buses headed towards Srebrenica, towards the base." That was at 26929. Just a quick follow-up on that, sir. Can you tell us where were you when you saw these buses?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when we gathered and boarded our bus, we encountered a couple of buses between Potocari and the base in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you know why they were heading towards the base, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this period of time before you boarded the buses, when you were standing in front of the base with your fellow PJP officers and had this clear view of this massive group of refugees, did you have any discussions with your fellow PJP officers about what was going to happen to them?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know Cvijan Vucinovic, sir? In 1995, he was a police officer from Milici and also a 1st Company Zvornik PJP officer. Cvijan Vucinovic. Does that name ring any bells with you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, he told the Sarajevo Prosecutor's Office, and this is at page 8 of his interview, and I quote: "On the day when I was in Potocari, shortly before our return to Bratunac, I saw buses arriving in Potocari. I knew the buses arrived there to take the Muslim population in the direction of Kladanj. At the time, I thought that was the safest solution for them to go to their territory because it was war." He also added, and I quote: "One feels the safest with his own people," and that he saw Serbian soldiers directing buses at the parking place, and he also saw people getting in one of those buses. Now, it's clear that he knew why those buses were there. Are you sure, sir, that you didn't here anything about the transportation of those civilians while you were there, and that you didn't see -- well, I'll take it one question at a time, please.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Just a couple more questions, sir, for you. I want to turn your attention to Sandici. When you got to Sandici, your platoon commander and the deputy company commander, Mr. Stuparevic, are there with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stuparevic was right next to me until the moment I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the -- your platoon commander was there as well; can you just confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole unit was there, including the platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you deployed anywhere from ten to 30 metres from each other; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the layout. There could have been five or ten metres between us, 15 at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, there's no dispute, sir, that you were wounded on that night between the 12th and the 13th of July. Can you just confirm what you told the SIPA investigators in your interview, and that is that there was moonlight on that night between the 12th and 13th?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, when asked about the source of light, since it was dark, it is possible that it was only moonlight. But that was the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. My question is, sir: As you sit here today, can you confirm what you told the SIPA investigators that your recollection is that there was moonlight that night?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He already said that it's possible, but I don't think you can get more than that, Mr. Thayer. Let's conclude, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, that was my last question, Mr. President. I wanted to see if he could confirm what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, given that it was dark, there is such a possibility that it was moonlight. I can't recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there re-examination, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just very, very limited number of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, we are nearing the end of your testimony. I would just like to clarify a few of your answers given to some of the questions posed by Mr. Thayer during cross-examination. My first question is this: Did your unit at all have any hand grenades when you went in the field and took part in the search of the terrain to the right of Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no infantry weapons except for our rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any other equipment? I don't mean only hand grenades but, say, mortars or anything of that nature. Did your unit have anything like that at its disposal?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During his examination, Mr. Thayer kept referring to the area from Zuti Most. I dare say it was his suggestion. But as you testified and as far as I can understand, did you set out from an area in front of Zuti Most, or from Zuti Most itself?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. The interpreters would like the witness to repeat his answer. Do you remember the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where we started from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Did you set out from an area in front of Zuti Most or from Zuti Most itself? What was your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In front of Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, interpreters for drawing our attention. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, during cross-examination, Mr. Thayer read out certain portions of some DutchBat soldier's statements, and I have a few questions about that. He said that the first group to appear was a group of 15 to 20 people who arrived at the DutchBat observation post. A young Serb soldier commanded the group, he had dark hair, around 185 centimetres in height, a bit red in the face, and spoke good English. I repeated this description. Bearing that in mind, could it be ascribed to any member of the PJP company Zvornik, in particular to any of the commanders?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next thing that Mr. Thayer read out was that there was a group wearing black uniforms that had dogs with them. I won't go back to the issue. You already said that you did not have any dogs. But as for the 1st PJP Zvornik Company, did you ever have black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the last category of soldiers Mr. Thayer referred to in his quotation. The third group which allegedly appeared wore blue camouflage uniforms. During your testimony, you talked about the fact that the police at the time -- when conducting regular duties wore blue camouflage uniforms. You were in the field at that moment. What uniform did you wear at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Green camouflage uniform with police insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Then it says that the people in blue camouflage uniforms were allegedly [In English] "a special police unit." [Interpretation] To the best of your recollection, did the special police ever wear blue camouflage uniforms during combat?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the fourth group. It says Rambo-types which wore a mix of civilian and military clothes, had good weapons, and sported knives and hand grenades. Did any of the members of the 1st PJP Company wear civilian clothes together with their uniforms, or were you all uniform in that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole unit wore green camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I suppose it doesn't mean much to you when I say "Observation Post Papa," but we could hear that it was the observation post that was between Zuti Most and Potocari. Witness Franken, who was one of the commanders of DutchBat and who testified before this Tribunal on the 17th of October 2006 as a Prosecution witness, he said the following, and I'll quote. It is page 2589 of the transcript in this case: [In English ] "... please, and tell us, how long did the member of the Dutch battalion stay in the Papa observation point near the Yellow Bridge? "A. I'm just thinking. Papa was withdrawn on the 13th or 14th, I don't know exactly, yes. "Q. And this withdrawal from the Papa observation point, did it follow your order, or did they do that on their own will? "A. No, a withdrawal is always done on order." Is this precisely what you said when you said that you carried out -- you did not carry out any attacks against the Papa observation post?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There was one other thing I wanted to quote. It is a Prosecutor's witness testimony of the 11th of January 2008, page 19459. Witness Joseph Kingori. Page 19459 lines 9 to 14: [In English] "Up until which point in time did DutchBat people remain there and when did they withdraw from their OP to the one near the Yellow Bridge?" And the answer was: "Your Honour, I think that was the last OP to be for the DutchBat to evacuate." [Interpretation] What I have just read, does this correspond with what you could see at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when they were withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for clarification of the record, based on the question my friend asked, when we speak about being in front of Yellow Bridge, can we just -- is it on the Srebrenica side or the Bratunac side, just so the record is clear about when we speak in front of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think it's very clear he drew the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... on that photograph that we showed to you where they stood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we need any further information. Do you have any questions? That brings us to the end of your testimony, sir. I'm very grateful for you to have accepted to come over as a witness for the Defence of Mr. Borovcanin. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish you a safe a journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, please have a chat, because I would like you to finish the next witness today. So you need to organise yourselves, even if it means that we have to do the exhibits process pertaining to the previous witness next time we meet. But we need to finish the next witness today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, have you insisted on having fresh air, Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. I was absolutely baffled, but Mr. Lazarevic explained the issue. I enjoy spending my breaks in there, General Gvero even more so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have been informed that there is agreement between you as regards the exhibits of the this last witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, for Mr. Bajagic and also for Mr. Zaric, so we can deal with this in a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That applies also to the Bajagic documents, exhibits? All right. Do we admit them all in other words, and MFI those which are pending translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct Mr. President, both Defence and Prosecution lists. You have our list. We have agreement that both lists go in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So that's how it will be. Thank you. All right. This is the whole list of the Borovcanin exhibits. They are all admitted with the caveat that I explained. These are the Prosecution ones, just four. They are also all admitted. Now we come to the last witness. The lists have been circulated as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no objections to any of the documents on the Borovcanin list, and we have no exhibits for that last witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So they are all admitted, and those which have not yet been translated will be MFI'd as I stated earlier. All right. Good morning to you, Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are most welcome to this Tribunal. You've been summoned as a Defence witness of the Borovcanin Defence team. Before you give testimony, you need to make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth. The text is being handed to you now, please read it out aloud, that will be your solemn commitment with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please make yourself comfortable. Mr. Lazarevic will ask you some questions, and then there will be some cross-examination, and hopefully you can go home. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We've met before, but just for the record, let me state my name. I'm Aleksandar Lazarevic, and together with the my colleagues, I represent the Defence of Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin before this Tribunal. Since this is the first time that you are testifying here, I'm asking you to wait for me to complete my question and then make a pause before you start answering, so that everything is record properly in the transcript. Could you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Nenad Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when and where you were born?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 9th of February 1966, in the village Zolja, Kalesija municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where you completed your primary education, and what are the schools did you attend?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I completed four grades in the place where I lived; and the remaining four grades in primary school and the high school, I completed in Kalesija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, before the war started in Bosnia, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I lived in Zolja, the place where I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was employed, and later on, I went to Pula in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, when the war started in Bosnia, did you leave your place, the place where you lived?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, on the 25th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The reason was the fact that the Muslim forces attacked my village and we all had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where did you go from Zolja?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I first moved to the Osmaci municipality, and from there to the Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, could you be more specific, when was it that you moved to the Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I moved to the Zvornik municipality on the 12th of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After you came to Zvornik, were you assigned to the reserve force of the police in the public security centre in Zvornik; and if so, could you please tell me when it was?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it did not happen immediately. I was first in the army; and then in 1993, I joined the reserve force of the police, of the Zvornik police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Just one more question in this vein: Do you work now; and if yes, can you please tell me where? What kind of work do you do?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I work in the Zvornik police station; I'm a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we now move to 1995. Could you tell me, what duties did you have in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I was a reserve police officer in the Zvornik police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please, tell me, in the discharge of the normal police duties, what uniforms were you issued?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we wore blue camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And as you went about the normal police business, did you also carry weapons; and if so, could you please tell us what kind of weapons did you carry?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I carried a pistol, 762. It was an official pistol we were all issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Could we now talk about the police station in Zvornik. Could you please tell me, as you went about your police business, who was your superior? How did the chain of command look?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The -- Goran Delic was the commander of the police station; the chief of the police department was Luka Bogdanovic; and Dragomir Vasic was the chief of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just one more question, as you went about police business, did you have an official ID card of any sort?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did have a badge and an official ID card.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Apart from the normal day-to-day police business, you were also a member of the PJP, were you not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, what company of the PJP did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the 1st PJP Company of the public security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. And now could you tell me, to the best of your recollection, how many companies there were, I mean the PJP companies in the Zvornik public security centre?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I think there were six.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You did indicate that you were in the 1st Company. Could you please tell me something about the structure, it's internal structure, how many elements that were?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It had three platoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Just a few questions about the PJP units. The 1st Company of the PJP, did it include only police officers from the Zvornik police station or from other police stations, too, or public security stations as they were called?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Personnel from other police stations: The Vlasenici, Milici, Bratunac, Sekovici, Skelani police stations, and also the Zvornik police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But all those police stations or public security centre that is we were talking about, did that belong to a centre in territorial terms?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: To the public security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. My microphone was off, so you couldn't hear me. When you were in the PJP and when your 1st Company was engaged in combat, could you please tell me, what kind of uniform you wore then as opposed to the uniform that you wore as you went about your day-to-day police business?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We wore grey camouflage uniform or green.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the record to be clear, it says grey and then green. It's one and the same, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a grey camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell, me when you were engaged in combat, did you carry weapons, other weapons in comparison to the weapons that you had as you went about your day-to-day business?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you went into combat, what kind of weapons did you carry?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We had automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have those pistols that you told us you were issued, the pistols that you carried when you went about your day-to-day business?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether the weapons that you used or that you carried when you took part in PJP operations, were those weapons the same for all of your members or did some people perhaps have some heavier weapons?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No. We all had automatic weapons, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you were in the PJP units participating in operations, did you have any communications equipment, radios, things like that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did have Motorolas. That's what we called them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did everybody is have Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, just the company commander, his deputy, and the platoon commanders, komandiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether the 1st PJP Company had a medical team of doctors and other medical personnel who would intervene if anything happened to anyone in the course of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me whether the 1st Company perhaps had a logistics platoon that would take care of providing supplies to the company personnel while they were in combat; food, ammunition, and other materiel?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, it had no such platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So when you as the 1st Company went out and took part in combat operations, who provided you with food? Who supplied you with ammunition and the other items that you needed in order to continue fighting?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It was the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the 1st PJP Company have its own mortar squad or any kind of artillery unit?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And did any members of the 1st PJP Company have mortars? Were they issued mortars or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, as you went on combat missions into the field, what kind of vehicles did you have?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We went there by bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the 1st Company have any kind of armoured vehicles to use when it went into combat?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, when you went into combat with the 1st PJP Company, did you use the white and blue vehicles with lights, of the kind that the police normally uses?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, did you, as a member of the 1st Company of the PJP of the Zvornik Security Services Centre, take part in combat even before July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when you were about to go into combat, could you please tell us, what kind of notice did you receive? Let's say, one day you were out and about doing your normal police job and how did it happen, then? How were you notified that you were supposed to go out and carry out operations as part of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I was at home, I would get a phone call. If I was on duty, then Motorolas were used, the ones that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now I would like to move on to 1995 and the events that preceded the Srebrenica events. In 1995, before the Srebrenica events, we know that they happened in July 1995, were you involved in any combat as the member of the 1st PJP?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, let us be quite specific, in June 1995, do you recall where was it that the 1st PJP Company participated in operations in combat?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in mid-June. We were at the Sarajevo Romanija front in Semizovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now I would like us to look at a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is in e-court and the number is 5D1321.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If it's easier for you, perhaps it would be a good idea to provide with you a hard copy of this document, so that you can have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mic is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The document is now in front of us. Please have a look at it, and I will have a few questions for you. First of all, it is a dispatch, sent by the chief of the Zvornik CJB on the 26th of June 1995, to the MUP RS Bijeljina, to the public and state security departments, to the police forces staff, to the SJB command, and all CJBs. You have seen this document during your proofing; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the third paragraph of the dispatch beginning with the words, "Given that the VRS forces could not retain the lost territory ..." It is the third paragraph. As you can see, it says that the SBP Doboj Detachment and the 1st PJP Company of the Zvornik PJP have been implementing a task in the area of Semizovac for ten days already. They were assigned to carry out a counterattack to regain the lost elevation points and push the enemy back. It say that is there was an attack on the 21st of June referred to in the first paragraph. Were you in the area of Semizovac, as would seem based on this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us go to the next paragraph, then, where the following thing is explained: The participation of the MUP units is explained, and it says that, during the combat, the 1st Company, 1st platoon of the PJP was wounded, Marinko Eric, and he was transferred to the VMA in Belgrade. To the best of your recollection, did this indeed happen? Was Marinko Eric wounded on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. He was wounded on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One last question concerning the document. In the last paragraph, it says: "The 3rd Company is at the lines reached given that the VRS no longer has sufficient forces to retain those locations, while the 1st Company is ready in Osmaci." Were you in Osmaci on the 21st of June, 1995, as specified here?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what it is that the company was on standby?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In case there was a renewed attack by the Muslim, we were supposed to intervene quickly and to move to the location of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, and I won't press you for any exact dates, until what time did the 1st Company remain in the area of Osmaci?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It remained there for a few days. I cannot recall exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We are done with the document, and I would like to move to the next one. You also had occasion to see that during your proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is 4D324.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is very easy to read the document, and I would kindly ask you to have a look at it on the screen and tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is an order sent by the chief of the police department of the CJB Zvornik, Luka Bogdanovic, of the 7th of July 1995; sent to the public security station in Bratunac, Milici, Vlasenici, Sekovici, and the police station in Zvornik, the police station for traffic safety in Zvornik, and the police station in Skelani. Do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I do.
