utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These PSs and SJBs referred to in the document, were they all part of the CJB of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are. They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Are all these SJBs and PSs supposed to provide their members for the 1st PJP Zvornik Company?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As of the 7th of July 1995, were the members of the PJP on standby in their respective police stations according to your recollection? I know you can't speak for the others, but you can say something for yourself and your colleagues in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were on standby in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What did that include or entail?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, we were supposed to intervene quickly if necessary to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: More or less, it is the same as we saw from the previous document when you were on standby in Osmaci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will no longer require the document. Let us move now to the events after the 10th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's first have a look at a document which bears the date the 10th of July 1995. It is an order of the staff commander number 64/95. In e-court it is 4D337. Let us have a look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As far as this document is concerned, you have already seen it before. It was sent to the commander of the special police brigade and other addressees. It is an order signed for staff commander, Tomislav Kovac. Let us look at the first paragraph. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can rather poorly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The first paragraph says: "Dedicate part of the MUP RS forces participating in combat in the Sarajevo theatre and sent as an independent unit to the area of Srebrenica in the course of tomorrow," which is the 11th of July. I'm also interested in item 2: "It should also comprise the 2nd Special Detachment of the police in Sekovici, the 1st Company of the PJP Zvornik, a mixed company of the joint forces of MUP and RSK of Serbia and the Republika Srpska, and the company from the training centre in Jahorina." The third item says: "I appoint Ljubisa Borovcanin, deputy commander of the special police brigade, to command the MUP units." My first question is this: In July 1995, when you went in the area of Srebrenica -- sorry, to participate in combat in Bratunac and further on, were you aware at the time that the 1st PJP Company was made part of a mixed unit?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin was appointed commander of such a mixed unit?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you know who Ljubomir Borovcanin was at all?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him. He was just an acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I used to see Mr. Borovcanin on occasion, I knew him by sight, I didn't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe it is sufficiently clear now. Let us not repeat what was already said in some other witness's testimonies. Let us now move directly to the point of departure in Zvornik. Can you tell us where you assembled in Zvornik and on what day?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We gathered in front of the Zvornik police station on the 11th of July 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximation, what time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I think in the early evening, in the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the transcript, it says the 11th of July 2002. Can you tell us what year it was?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The 11th of July 2005 -- sorry, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's okay. You gathered there -- well, I don't want to put words in your mouth. But did you have any vehicles; if so, which and where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Once gathered in front of the station, we set off on buses towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were there also members of the 1st PJP Company who were not from the police station on Zvornik on board the bus? Here, I mean the traffic safety police station and others.

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: With us, it was only members of the PS Zvornik and the traffic police station in Zvornik, because we comprised the 1st Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you told where you were to go?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We were told to go to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn anything specific about it, except for the fact that you were to go to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing else was said except for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On your journey to Bratunac, did you stop anywhere?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We stopped in Konjevic Polje. There we were joined by certain members from Vlasenici and Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions concerning Konjevic Polje. Was there a police checkpoint in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was, a civilian police checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Were there any other police companies' members that you could see in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Not at that time. I didn't see anyone save for the members of my company and the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Approximately, when did you arrive in Bratunac on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in Bratunac, I think, between 6.00 and 7.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you left Zvornik, did you bring along any combat equipment, and if so, what?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I carried my automatic rifle and five clips. It is standard for combat ammo kit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any additional food, you as the 1st PJP Company members?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We received none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you got to Bratunac, where did you got off the bus?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We got off in front of the police -- of the public security station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you accompanied by any officers of the 1st PJP Company?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We were accompanied by the deputy of the 1st Company, Radislav Stuparevic, and the 1st Platoon commander, Cvijan Ristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was Radomir Pantic with you on the bus?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you arrive in front of the police station in Bratunac. What happened next? Were you told about what was going on?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in front of the station, we were waited there by the 1st Company commander, Radomir Pantic, and some members of the 1st Company. Up to that point, I didn't know what was going on in Srebrenica before I came to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, how did things develop? Where were you billeted, if at all?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That evening we were billeted in a school, in a gym of that school. Commander Pantic told us to stick together, not to wander away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July 1995, did you receive any specific tasks?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We were only told that there was a possibility we would be moving to the Zuti Most area, but that was to be the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, when did you first hear that the VRS forces had entered Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It was that evening when I arrived in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was there any talk? Did people know what was happening with the troops from Srebrenica, to be quite specific with the BH Army groups?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nobody knew where they were, what they were doing. They were probably in the woods around that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at the next document in e-court. That's P3110.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is a bulletin of daily events of the Zvornik public security centre. The date is the 11th or the 12th of July 1995. Could you please look at page 2 of this document entitled "Combat Operations."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You can see here it says "Combat Operations." That's item number 1. Could you please look at the third paragraph in this bulletin or report. It says here: "In the course of the day," that would be the 11th, "the 1st PJP of the public security centre from Zvornik was sent to this frontline at 1830, while the other defence lines in the Visin [phoen], Vukovina area is manned by the 4th Company of the CJB PJP with 81 police officers; whereas, the Konjevic Polje and Han Pogled areas, there is the 6th Company of the CJB PJP with 52 police officers?" Let me now go through some items regarding this bulletin. It says that the 1st Company was sent at 1830 hours. To the best of your recollection, is that the time when you headed out of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can see here, in this paragraph, that it is indicated that other lines in the Visin-Vukovina areas, the 4th Company of the SJB Zvornik PJP, and that in Konjevic Polje and Han Pogled, there is the 6th Company. You, as the 1st Company, did you have anything to do with the two companies that are mentioned in this bulletin?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No. We had nothing to do with the 4th and the 6th company.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. You spent the night, as you've already told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We won't be needing this document anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You spent the night in the gym, as you described to us. Could you please tell us what happened then, in the morning of the 12th? When did you wake up? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th, we got up before dawn, between 4.00 and 5.00. I can't remember exactly. Then we were put on buses and we were taken to the Zuti Most area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, your bus stopped in front of the Zuti Most. Could you please tell me, at the time when you reached this area in front of Zuti Most, could you please tell us what was the weather like.

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was foggy. The visibility was poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you and your unit got off the bus. Could you please tell us whether Commander Pantic was there with you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Commander Pantic was there with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did he arrive on the bus or on his own?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: He was on the bus with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: As you got off the bus there, did you notice any medical support elements there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I saw an ambulance which was close to this place where we got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, apart from your company, was there anybody else there that did not belong to your company and but you were able to see them, a soldier for instance?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I think there was a soldier from the Bratunac Brigade, I think. I don't know whether he was a deminer or what. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So, tell me, as you got off the bus, were you told your mission?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Commander Pantic told us that we were to search the area to the left of Zuti Most, heading towards a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Could you please tell me, as you were in this area in front of Zuti Most, were you able to see Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could see him that morning. He was with my commander, Mr. Pantic. They were some 20 or 30 metres away from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So could you tell us, what were you able to observe? What was Mr. Borovcanin doing?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin was talking to my commander, Mr. Pantic. I don't know what they were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Could you please tell us, how did things proceed? Where was your unit headed?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We headed to the area to the right of Zuti Most in single file, and we were accompanied by this deminer. It was his task to lead us through the minefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what happened then?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This soldier led some dozen members of the 1st Company through the minefield, and on the way back, he stepped on to a mine and he was seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let me ask you a couple of follow-up questions. Did you receive any information whether any UN forces were deployed in that area?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Before heading out to conduct the search operation, Commander Pantic told us that from Zuti Most onwards, there was a checkpoint, an UNPROFOR checkpoint, but we couldn't see it because it was foggy, and that we should not open fire or do anything else against this UNPROFOR point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let us move on. So your unit is heading out in single file, there was this incident in which this young man was wounded. I assume that this kept you there for awhile?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So please proceed, tell me what happened next?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: After that, we made a detour around this minefield and then we spread out, and when we entered the village, we encountered some trenches and connecting trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you encounter any resistance by the Muslim forces in the course of this search operation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Not in this village. There was no resistance. In fact, we did not encounter any armed groups. We did not encounter any civilians in that village either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Had you received any orders concerning civilians?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from Commander Pantic. If we were to encounter any armed groups, if they offered resistance, then we were to deal with it in a military way; and if we encountered civilians, we were not to touch them. We were to leave them where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to complete your evidence today, I would like to speed up now. We don't want to have to recall you or make you stay here longer. So, after the search operation was completed, once you ascertained that there was nobody there, civilians or military personnel, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We carried out the search of that area and we got up on to a hill, an elevation; and since we didn't find anyone in the village, we received an order to move down towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you got down from that hill, the elevation that you reached in the course of the search operation. So where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We got down to the tarmac road leading towards Srebrenica. It's the Bilici-Bratunac road leading to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How long -- how far were you from the UN base, if you were at a distance at all? How far was that location where you were on the road?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't be very specific because I really didn't know where it was, so I couldn't give you the exact location where we got on the road. I think maybe 30 to 50 metres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I will not belabour the point. From that place where you were, were you able to see the UN base, the DutchBat base?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When we got down on to the road, I could see the Dutch soldiers who were guarding the civilians who were in a factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself approach the civilians?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I did not approach the civilians at all. I wasn't even on the road itself. We were on the other side of the road. The factory was on the other side, and I didn't cross the road at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But do you know if anyone else from your unit perhaps approached the civilians?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. How long did you remain there, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I and a few of my colleagues remained there for maybe ten or 15 minutes tops.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During that time, did you have an opportunity to observe the arrival of any transport vehicles, such as, for instance, buses or trucks?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did see some buses and trucks arriving and going down to the factory where the civilians were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While you were there and while you were able to observe what was happening with this large group of refugees, were you able to observe any violence against them, were you able to observe that men were being separated from women, things of that nature?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. So the bus came to pick you up and you went away. Could you please tell us, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When the bus arrived, we boarded the bus and we went to Bratunac. We got off the bus in front of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Did you remain there at the time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We did spend sometime there. I don't know how long it was. Perhaps four or five hour, something like that. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, where did your unit go after that, after this stay in front of the Bratunac police station?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: After maybe four or five hours, as I've already indicated, Pantic, Commander Pantic told us that we were to go to the Sandici area. We boarded the buses and we drove off towards Sandici. Up until that time I didn't know the place at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So that's what you did, you just went on?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you reached Sandici?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We reached Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So this place, Sandici, where you were deployed, did you know that place from before, or was that the first time that you got there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, I did not know that place at all. This was the first time that I was in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you reached this area, and how did things unfold once you got off the bus?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We got off the bus. Commander Pantic deployed us from this house that was partly destroyed downhill towards Konjevic Polje, and so we were deployed in this manner in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was there a pattern to your deployment? Were you all in one place?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, we were not all in one place. We were spaced apart maybe ten or 15 minutes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a few more questions about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just correct for the record. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you what your task was when you were deployed there in the area of this road?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Commander Pantic told us that the Muslim forces might attempt to break through and to cut the road, and it was our task to prevent them because that would endanger the Serb population behind our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What time of day was it when you arrived in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in the early evening, between 6.00 and 7.00 or 8.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The place at which you were deployed, could you see what the traffic was behind you from that point?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I could see it, we were right next to the road, buses were passing by. Several buses with civilians passed by with UNPROFOR escort. There were a number of transport and passenger vehicles that passed by as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe a bus convoy?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the sense of who was on the buses, could you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I did see a convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. You've already answered that. My mistake. I should have been following the transcript more carefully. What followed in the course of the night of the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the night in front of us in the woods, one could hear firing on several occasions, firing from firearms, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you engaged in combat during that night? Did you open fire? Were you fired upon before the next morning?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We did not open fire until the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During the night between the 12th and the 13th of July, did you take any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the record, the question was: "Did you open fire at all during the night in the direction from which you could hear the firing?"

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No. We did not open fire until the next morning at 3.00 or 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In your own words, could you explain to us what happened the next morning around 3.00 or 4.00?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Between 3.00 or 4.00, there was firing, the Muslim forces attacked our positions, there were several explosions, and I was wounded on that occasion, as well as my mate, Zarko Zaric and Nenad Andric. A guy from Bratunac was killed as well, I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I understand that you cannot recall that. Can you tell us, where did the attack come from?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It came from an area that was in front of us from the hill and the woods. We were positioned on [indiscernible] towards that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your assessment, to the extent you were able to see, how long did the attack last?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: For about ten minutes, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You have told us already that you were injured then. Can you tell us what happened to you subsequently? Were you taken anywhere?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I was put in a vehicle, although I don't remember which, and taken to the health centre in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look next at a document that is in e-court. It is 4D51892 [as interpreted], which is a logbook of the Bratunac healthcare centre, dated the 13th of July 1995. It seems the number is incorrect. It is 4DP1892. The page I need has ERN number 0179-3918. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The second column from the top, the second row from the top: "1484, the 13th of July 1995, 4.45." In the next column, can we see your name and your father's name?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this guy was hospitalized. Let's be practical please and let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: There's no dispute about that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell me, how long did you stay at the Bratunac health centre?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I spent an hour there or so, and then I was taken to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What happened in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In Zvornik, I was merely checked and referred to Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you, indeed, taken to Loznica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and I was treated there for about a fortnight. On my request, I was discharged for home treatment, home care.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What were your injuries? We seem to have omitted that.

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I was injured to my head; my face and my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'd like us to have a look at another document which is 4D555. We do not have a translation. We have asked for it but are still awaiting it. It is a medical record, and we did not dare produce an unofficial translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what is the importance of this part of the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Only to find out the period in which the witness was in Serbia for healing, because it dates from the 13th to the 25th of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just put it to him. "Were you in Serbia for this reason on such a day and such a day?" Then we finish there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I will do that. I will have just a couple of more questions and that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, from the document, we can see that you were treated at the eye ward in Loznica between 13th of July and 25th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, that is the correct period?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like us to have a look at another document which is 503113 [as interpreted]. [In English] P03113. It's not 5, it's P. Sorry. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As you know, this is a bulletin similar to the one you saw already, a bulletin of daily events of the Zvornik public security centre for the 13th and 14th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you see where it says "Combat Operations"? It says: "In the morning of the 13th of July 1995, large groups of enemy military formations from Srebrenica infiltrated ..." I won't go on reading the paragraph, but I'm interested in this part: "In the course of the fighting in these places, police officer Zeljko Ninkovic was killed from the public security station; Milos Zoljic, Zarko Zaric, and Nenad Andric were seriously wounded; while Nenad Filipovic was lightly wounded." Does this tally with what, indeed, took place?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in one name. I see that in addition to the three of you who were wounded in Sandici and Zeljko Ninkovic for whom we know was killed, the name of Milos Zoljic appears as well. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: He is a cousin of mine, and I believe he was with the 6th company. He was wounded in Konjevic Polje, as I learned later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To conclude, I have a few questions left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. In transcript, we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us again, Milos Zoljic was a member of which company?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The 6th, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Where was he wounded?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In Konjevic Polje. I learned that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Upon return from treatment, how long did you stay on sick leave?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a month and a half or two. I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I only have a few questions about your former statements. Have you given any statements to the various organs of the police, investigative judges, or an agency of any kind?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I gave -- I have given two statements to the police, one in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you give all those statements prior to meeting with the Defence of Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During your proofing, you could see those statements for the first time since you were shown those statements by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, when those statements were being drafted, were you able to read them before signing them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I gave the first ones -- the first two in Zvornik and Bijeljina. As for the Sarajevo statement, I was able to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify something, regarding the first two statements in Zvornik and Bijeljina, were you able to read them before signing them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I did not read them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think the transcript remains unclear. When you gave the statements, did you then read them before signing them; that is to say, not yesterday or the day before when we were proofing you for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. During the proofing, you pointed out a number of mistakes you were able to observe in those two statements, and there were some slight incorrections in the third statement you provided?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No question for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Nothing, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I won't be able to finish before the break, but I will definitely finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My name is Nelson Thayer, I'll be asking you a few questions on behalf of the Prosecution. The first thing I want to do is show you just two photographs and see if you can help us place some names to a couple of faces. You told the Prosecutor's investigators in Sarajevo that when you went to Bratunac with your PJP platoon, Rista Ikonic and Mile Savic were with you. Can you confirm that those two Zvornik police officers were with you for this mission?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't want to interrupt. We still haven't got the list from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It should be on its way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Do you prefer if because I prefer to stick to what is the best practice. If you prefer to stop here for the time being until you receive the list and Mr. Thayer continues after the break, we can do that. We can have the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's fine with the Prosecution, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We would prefer to have the list before Mr. Thayer starts that was the practice for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's been sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have the 25 minute break now. Thank you. --- Break taken at 12.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you some very quick video clips, and I have some still photographs from the video, just so see if you can help us with two identifications of people who were at Sandici at the same time you were. Okay? So if you can just watch your monitor and we'll see some footage in a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: For the record, this is from P02047, the trial video, 2 hours 37 minutes 50 seconds. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, we've paused it at 2 hours 38 minutes 7.1 seconds. If your image is as blurry as mine is, I'm going to give you that photo still. There are two individuals depicted in this photograph. I'm asking you whether you can recognise the younger one on the left with the overalls wrapped around waist.

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recognise this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. We'll be done with this exhibit. I'm going to show you another clip taken near the destroyed white house at Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, there are three men in this picture. The man on the far right has been identified by Mile Savic as himself, and I'm going to show you the video still photograph. First of all, can you confirm, sir, that that is Mile Savic on the far right, with the mustache, walking basically out of the shot?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is Mile Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And my question to you, sir: There is a gentleman in the middle of these three also in a camouflage uniform. Please take a look at that photograph. Can you identify that person for us? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know who this soldier is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We are at 2 hours 52 minutes 32.5 seconds, and we are done.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, just moving along, sir, you testified that you did not bring your service pistol with you in the field. How about hand grenades, did you have any hand grenades with you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't, or at least I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. There was an interview of a third platoon PJP officer. His name is Srdjan Milosevic. He was the komandir of the 3rd Section of the 3rd Platoon, a police officer from Bratunac. Do you know Srdjan Milosevic, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know him by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: He told the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo that he brought with him on this mission his automatic rifle, two hand grenades, four ammunition clips for his rifle, a 7.65 millimetre pistol, and his camouflage jumpsuit, and that was for this specific mission. Just ask you to search your recollection again, sir, do you think you might be wrong when you testified that no one had service pistols or hand grenades with them in the field on this mission?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that nobody had. I say that I myself didn't carry any hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There was one piece of evidence missing here in his answer. He says: "I didn't know. I didn't say that nobody had. I don't know." That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, did your uniform that you wore in the field have a particular patch?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a patch worn on the left shoulder. It said "police."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you remember whether it said anything else or just "policija"?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing else, just "policija."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, taking you to the search of the terrain in the morning of 12 July, as you approached Potocari, who was near you during this search? Who from your platoon or your company, if your platoon had been split up at all, do you recall being near you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really recall. A long time has elapsed, so I couldn't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you also told the SIPA investigators in Sarajevo, that Commander Pantic had told you that Potocari was an inhabited area with houses, but, and I'm quoting now from your statement - and this is at page 8 of the English and page 5 of the B/C/S - I quote: "We did not find anybody in those houses but we knew that Muslims lived in there." Can you confirm, sir, that those houses were, in fact, searched that morning; and if so, by whom?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Whether they went into the houses or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, when you told the Prosecutor's office in Sarajevo that "We did not fine anybody this those houses," my question to you is: Who went in the houses to determine that there was nobody in them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who went in. I did not get into any of the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you aware that other people with you on this search of the terrain did go into the houses, even though you might not have been near them?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He already answered this question, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, he hasn't answered that particular question. I'm following up on his prior answer. He say "I don't know who went in. I did not get into any of houses."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if he doesn't know who went in, how do you expect him to answer this question any further?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If he has any awareness of anybody going in, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I told you, he already said "I don't know who went in." So --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one final touch to it. You didn't go inside any of these houses, you don't know who went into these houses, but do you know that someone did go into these houses, although you don't know who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who or whether went in at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you see any dogs accompanying any of the Serb forces who were scouring the terrain towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any dogs.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you got closer to the UN compound where this massive crowd of civilians had gathered, did you stay in one place once you got down there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't stay there. As soon as we got down to the tarmac road, we headed towards Bratunac on foot. It's about 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you told the investigators in Sarajevo - this is at page 8 of the English and page 5 of the B/C/S - you told them that you saw that buses had arrived and that the Muslim civilians from that factory complex were boarding them. Can you confirm that you saw this, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that there is a proofing note, and my colleague is well aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Answer the question please, Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see that they were starting to board, but as I move towards Bratunac, I could see the buses with civilians pass by.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you didn't see any separations, though, is that your testimony; that is, males being separated from their families?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you 65 ter 3803. I just want to ask you some specific questions about the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo on 8 October 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 9 of the English and page 5 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you had a chance to look at this most recently with my learned friends before your proofing, and I understand it from the proofing note that you only had two minor corrections. One is that the buses with the population were going in the direction of Bratunac, which you saw while on your way to Bratunac; and that there's a reference later on to buses passing by non-stop when you are at Sandici, but you wish to correct that there was traffic and there was different vehicles passing by, but not that it was non-stop. Does that fairly capture the only two changes you wanted to make after you reviewed the statement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at paragraph 9 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we're going to have to -- sorry, page 9 of the English and page 5 of the B/C/S. We are looking at paragraph 5, which continues from the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You stated that, and I quote: "The buses that arrived to Potocari made a U-turn at the factory, and when the people embarked the buses, they drove away in the direction of Bratunac. I knew that all those people would be transferred to Kladanj in those buses. I knew that because we had been told so." Do you see that in your statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question to you is: Who told you that the population was going to be transported to Kladanj that morning?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't tell you. That somebody was saying that, but I can't give you the name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, before we move on to Sandici, sir, I just want to put a couple of propositions to you. The first is that we have statements from numerous witnesses, such as UNPROFOR Dutch soldiers, who were either at the checkpoint near Yellow Bridge or who were watching what was happening from a distance. These statements detail how the Dutch checkpoint near Yellow Bridge was disarmed by Serb forces, how the communications in that checkpoint were disabled, and how the Dutch soldiers there were not free to leave. Do you know anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We also have statements from numerous witnesses, including more DutchBat UN soldiers, that as the Serb forces advanced down from the area of Yellow Bridge towards Potocari, that those Serb forces were cleansing the houses with grenades and dogs. Do you know anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to Sandici for just a few more questions. You testified that you waited for a period of time in Bratunac after being driven there from Potocari, and that you were then ordered to be deployed along the Konjevic Polje Road; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive an order to go on to Zvornik, or was your order only to be deployed on that road in the area of Sandici?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Just to deploy along the road at Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we could go back to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I don't know if it's still on e-court. Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You also told the Sarajevo Prosecutor's Office that, and I quote: "We were also told that there were armed Muslims moving through the forest and posing a threat. They would cut off the road communication between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje, and, by doing so, putting the Serbian population in a threatened position and preventing passage of buses with civilians from Potocari." My question is simple, sir: Do you stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we received the order to prevent the road from being blocked lest there should be any threat to the Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you also say in this statement, in addition to preventing the threat to the Serb population, preventing passage of buses with civilians from Potocari. Who was the source of that information, sir? Was that Commander Pantic, or was that somebody else that was part of the reason for your deployment?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't really answer this question. I don't know who told you [as interpreted] that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Filipovic, Mr. Filipovic? If you could come closer to the microphones, please, and raise your voice a little bit because the interpreters are having problems. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, this may be --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one small correction for the transcript. On page 72, it's line 20, "... who told me that." It's line 18, or maybe 20, I don't know. We have a different transcript one on the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I thank my friends. That's exactly what I was going to try to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you say "I don't know who told me that," what you are telling the Trial Chamber is you don't recall who told you that preventing the passage of buses with civilians from Potocari was one of the concerns that prompted your deployment to that road?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall who told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified about being deployed -- I'm sorry. You, I believe, told the prosecutor's office in Sarajevo that you were deployed next to a house, and that the 2nd Detachment of the special police brigade was deployed from the area of that house towards Bratunac. Can you confirm that that is an accurate statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was that one of the destroyed houses, or was that a destroyed house that I think you may have mentioned earlier; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That's the house that was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you also told the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo that Commander Pantic, and I quote - and this is page 10 of the English, page 6 of the B/C/S - I quote: "... informed us that in the case the Muslims appear and carry out an armed attack, we were to reply in the same way and to engage them in battle. If they would not attack us but start to surrender, we were supposed to escort them to Bratunac. I do not know where exactly were they to be escorted to and to whom." Do you stand by that answer that you gave in your interview as well, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One single question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, it appears to me that there is something left unclear after the question that you were asked about the passage of the convoy. Did anyone, at the time when you were given a task and deployed there, did anyone tell you about the convoy that was supposed to pass through?

utterances.speaker: NENAD FILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody told us anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Filipovic, we are finished with your testimony. You are free to go back home. Our staff will assist you. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony and I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Documents, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Two documents, Your Honour. Let me just take a look. Three -- two only, I'm sorry: 4D555, it's a medical report; and P3110, it's CJB Zvornik Bulletin number 193/95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the first one, translation is still pending.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President, and we have no documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So these documents are admitted. I take it there are no objections from anyone else. Before we adjourn, there are two things. One is Borovcanin motion that has not been objected to at, which we can dispose of orally. You will recall that on the 3rd of October -- or before the 3rd of October, the Borovcanin Defence team had asked for seeking admission pursuant to rule 92 bis of the statements of Dr. Petar Loncarevic, and the transcript of the testimony of Krsto Simic, and Blagojevic and Jokic. The Prosecution, as I said, has not objected, and having gone through the details of the motion, we consider that the evidence of both Loncarevic and that of Krsto Simic meets the requirements of 92 bis. So we are granting the motion providing the following: Namely, that the Borovcanin Defence team -- in other words, the motion is being granted on these conditions: That the Borovcanin Defence team provides the statement of Petar Loncarevic in a form that fully complies with Rule 92 bis; and, secondly, that the same Defence team provides the exhibits referred to in the transcript of the testimony of Krsto Simic, because otherwise we will not be in a position to follow. The other thing is you will have certainly noticed that the Appeals Chamber dismissed in its entirety the Popovic appeal against our decision on motion to re-open the Prosecution case. The decision of the Appeals Chamber came on the 24th of September. Now, in that decision -- in our decision of the 9th May, we had granted the Prosecution motion of the 7th April, in which the Prosecution had sought to re-open its case for the purpose of presenting the evidence of three witnesses. I don't need to go into details. During the 65 ter conference which was held on the 20th of May and the Pre-Defence conference of the 22nd of May of this year, the Prosecution and the Popovic Defence teams were requested to discuss the procedural arrangement that would be needed for re-opening the Prosecution case. At the 65 ter conference, the parties were told that the Trial Chamber would prefer that the witnesses be called for examination-in-chief and cross-examination at the same time. Since the decision of the Trial Chamber has now been confirmed by the appeals Chamber, we are proposing to you, Mr. Zivanovic, and to you, Mr. McCloskey, to update us, unless you have already reached an agreement, on how you intend to organise the presentation of evidence of these three witnesses, to be followed then by any witnesses that you may wish to call in view of these. So Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have he had some discussions with my learned friend. Basically asked him when he would prefer that that evidence go on. My understand is that the preference is that it go on at the end of the Defence cases presentations, and we are fine with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, do you wish to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I just wanted to confirmation from you. All right. Any other business you wish to transact? None. We stand adjourned. Thank you.
